requirements.requirement: Keep application data under /srv/data recoverable through filesystem snapshots.
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem was created at /srv/data, a read-only device-mapper snapshot was successfully captured, and the snapshot retained the original hashes while live data changed. The backing filesystem and service also recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: After modifying the directory, restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: The executor recorded the baseline structure, permissions, ownership, symlink target, sizes, and file hashes; then changed and deleted baseline objects and added a new file. Snapshot merge restored a manifest identical to baseline, recovered the deleted file and symlink, and removed the post-snapshot file.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Direct observations before implementation and after restoration and reboot consistently show RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The exercised device-mapper snapshot targets and XFS tooling functioned on that installed platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates snapshot creation, bounded live-data modification, exact restoration, persistence through reboot, and preservation of the legacy OS and kernel. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, mount, device mapping, and data were all observed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-database consistency could not be independently assessed.

The exact-restore comparison directly covers object structure, types, permissions, ownership, sizes, symlink target, and file hashes, but does not separately enumerate extended attributes, ACLs, or timestamps.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation and corrective mutations had clear task-related roles, and the temporary device-mapper prototype was fully removed. No failed services or new listening exposure remained. The only unnecessary retained mutations were four low-risk temporary evidence artifacts that were not cleaned up: /tmp/restored.manifest, /tmp/pre-reboot.manifest, /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, and /tmp/post-reboot.manifest.
